tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: YellowStorm is an AI Agent Chat Platform with real-time streaming. It consists of a NestJS backend, React frontend, Python agent runtime (ADK), and vector store service. This tour walks through the core architecture.
tour.languageLesson: This monorepo uses three languages: TypeScript (NestJS + React), Python (ADK runtime), and Protocol Buffers (gRPC contracts). The backend communicates with the ADK via gRPC, and the frontend connects via SSE/REST.

tour.title: Backend Architecture
tour.description: The NestJS backend serves REST APIs to the frontend and communicates with the ADK via gRPC. It uses MongoDB for persistence and Passport JWT for authentication.
tour.languageLesson: NestJS uses decorators (@Module, @Controller, @Injectable) and dependency injection. Each feature is organized into modules with controllers (routes), services (logic), and schemas (MongoDB).

tour.title: Backend Feature Modules
tour.description: Feature modules encapsulate domain logic. Key modules: conversation (AI chat), workspace (documents), auth (JWT), admin (user management), playbook (agent workflows).

tour.title: gRPC Contract Layer
tour.description: The Protocol Buffer schema defines the contract between the NestJS backend and the Python ADK service. This is the critical cross-boundary interface.
tour.languageLesson: The proto file defines the gRPC service interface. The NestJS backend acts as gRPC client, the ADK as gRPC server. Important: @grpc/proto-loader does NOT auto-convert plain JS objects to Struct wire format.

tour.title: Frontend Architecture
tour.description: React 18 frontend with Vite build tool, Zustand state management, Radix UI components, and Tailwind CSS. Uses i18next for localization.

tour.title: Frontend Feature Modules
tour.description: Each feature has its own module with API client, store (Zustand), types, components, and locale files. Key modules: conversation, workspace, admin, auth, playbook.

tour.title: ADK Agent Runtime
tour.description: The Python ADK service runs AI agents using LangGraph. It receives gRPC requests from the backend, orchestrates agent workflows, and streams responses back.
tour.languageLesson: The ADK uses LangGraph for agent orchestration. Agents are defined as state machines with nodes (processing steps) and edges (transitions). Google ADK provides the agent framework.

tour.title: Infrastructure & Deployment
tour.description: Docker configurations for local development and deployment. The backend, ADK, and vector store each have their own containerization.
